# GitHub Copilot Billing Exploit

## Summary
GitHub Copilot's current billing model charges a flat rate for up to 1,500 messages regardless of token usage, leading to potential abuse by users who can run extremely expensive queries within one message. This exploit was highlighted when @theo demonstrated running over 60 million tokens in a single request costing around $30.

## Key insights
- **Billing Model Vulnerability**: The flat-rate per-message billing model allowed for substantial cost savings and inefficiencies, as users could leverage it to run extensive queries that would otherwise be prohibitively expensive.
- **Exploitation Techniques**: Users found ways to keep sessions open indefinitely by using subagents or prompting the AI to ask follow-up questions after completing tasks. This prevented messages from finishing and continued token usage without additional premium requests.
- **Impact on Providers**: The model's unsustainable economics forced GitHub Copilot to transition to a per-token billing system starting June 1st, addressing the abuse issues but also ending the era of generous cost structures for power users.

## Discussion
The debate around this exploit highlights the challenges in pricing AI services that can be abused by advanced users. While flat-rate models offer simplicity and ease-of-use for casual users, they are vulnerable to exploitation by those who understand how to maximize their utility through technical means. This incident underscores the need for more sophisticated billing mechanisms that accurately reflect the true cost of service usage.

## Open questions
- How will other AI providers adapt their pricing strategies in response to similar vulnerabilities?
- What measures can be taken to prevent abuse while still offering accessible and affordable services to all users?
